source: OTRF/Security-Datasets datasets/compound/apt29/emulationplans/apt29.xlsx (MITRE ATT&CK Evaluations APT29 emulation plan)
note: Condensed by hand from the real emulation-plan spreadsheet (stage/step/technique/source/target columns) into a compact attack-chain shape. Verbose hands-on command text and credentials were dropped; step IDs, stages, MITRE technique IDs, and source/target hosts are preserved as-is from the source.

steps.description: User clicks an executable masquerading as a document; payload opens a C2 connection over port 1234.
Attacker spawns interactive cmd.exe and powershell.exe via the C2 connection.
Searches the filesystem for documents/media, collects and compresses them into a single archive.
Staged archive exfiltrated over the existing C2 connection.
Uploads an image file with a concealed PowerShell script.
UAC bypass executes the hidden payload; new HTTPS C2 connection established on port 443.
Enumerates running processes to find/kill the original access, then deletes associated files.
Wide recon sweep via a single discovery script, partly via Windows API calls.
Creates a new Windows service for persistent access.

techniques: T1060 Registry Run Keys / Startup Folder
steps.description: Drops a payload into the Startup folder as a second persistence mechanism.
Harvests browser-stored credentials using a renamed/masquerading tool.
Dumps password hashes from the host.
LDAP-enumerates domain hosts, opens a remote PowerShell session to a second victim.
New payload executed on the second victim via PsExec using stolen credentials.
Second victim's files collected, encrypted, compressed, and exfiltrated over C2.

techniques: T1060 Registry Run Keys / Startup Folder
steps.description: Original victim reboots; both persistence mechanisms fire, giving a fresh callback.

techniques: T1060 Registry Run Keys / Startup Folder
steps.description: Second-day scenario: user clicks a link file; hidden ADS payload sandbox-checks, persists via Run key, and opens an HTTPS C2 channel.
UAC bypass yields a high-integrity callback.
Downloads and runs Mimikatz via a custom WMI class to dump plaintext credentials.
Dumped credentials used to open a remote PowerShell session to the domain controller.
Copies Mimikatz to the domain controller and dumps the KRBTGT account hash.
Forges a Kerberos Golden Ticket from the KRBTGT hash, opens a remote session, and creates a new domain account.
